title: The Sharper of Alexandria and the Chief of Police

keywords: the sharper of alexandria and the chief of police
full_text:
The Chief of Police of Alexandria was a pompous official who boasted at every public gathering that no thief, sharper, or pickpocket in all of Egypt could outwit his guards or enter his fortified residence. 'My house is an iron fortress,' he proclaimed. 'My watchmen never sleep, my hounds never tire, and my locks are forged by the finest smiths in Cairo.'

A witty sharper of Alexandria heard these boasts and felt his professional pride challenged. He sent a polite message to the chief: 'Tomorrow night, O Chief, I shall steal your favorite horse from your stable and your personal silver basin from your bedroom, and I shall leave you a basket of onions in exchange!'

The police chief laughed in fury, doubled his guards, stationed ten armed watchmen around the stable, and placed four guards outside his bedroom door, sleeping with his naked sword upon the mattress.

At midnight, a cold, drizzling rain set in. A wandering peddler carrying a heavy earthen jar of warm spiced lentil soup and a skin of sweetened cordial knocked upon the courtyard gate, begging for shelter from the tempest. The shivering guards, freezing in the rain, gladly welcomed the peddler, who generously offered them bowls of hot soup and cups of sweet cordial.

Unknown to the guards, the cordial was steeped with a harmless herbal sleeping draught. Within an hour, every guard in the courtyard and corridor was snoring peacefully!

The sharper, throwing off his peddler's disguise, walked quietly into the stables, saddled the chief’s favorite grey mare, and tied a basket of fresh red onions to the manger. He then tiptoed into the bedroom, removed the silver washbasin from the stand beside the snoring chief, placed an onion in its center, and rode out through the open gates.

At dawn, the humiliated chief woke to the smell of onions and the silence of his guards. Realizing the sharper had fulfilled every word of his promise without shedding a drop of blood, the chief abandoned his haughty boasts, learning that true security is built on quiet diligence rather than loud arrogance.
moral: Vigilance requires constant humility; he who boasts of his security will be outsmarted by a watchful eye.
